Deprecated prometheus request meta-metrics have been removed (http_request_duration_microseconds, http_request_duration_microseconds_sum, http_request_duration_microseconds_count, http_request_size_bytes, http_request_size_bytes_sum, http_request_size_bytes_count, http_requests_total, http_response_size_bytes, http_response_size_bytes_sum, http_response_size_bytes_count) due to removal from the prometheus client library. ```

issue_context.title: Update to etcd 3.4 in Kubernetes 1.17 release
issue_context.body:
follow the same pattern that we updated to 3.3.15:
- client side changes needs to be vendored in (similar to https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/81434)
- update default etcd server (similar to https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/82199)
comments: Let's please do this early in the release cycle. And it should not be that difficult ™️, just mechanical changes following the pattern of the 2 PRs above.
@dims +1. Are you planning to work on it? Or I can do it.
random question: how are these things updated? How are PRs such as https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/83209 generated?

@alejandrox1 I am following [Adding or updating a dependency](https://github.com/kubernetes/community/blob/master/contributors/devel/sig-architecture/vendor.md#adding-or-updating-a-dependency) to update etcd.
/assign @jingyih as you mentioned you would like to update etcd server side to 3.4.3.

Sounds good. I will work on updating default etcd server to 3.4.3.

/assign

review_comments:
cc @kubernetes/sig-instrumentation-pr-reviews @brancz  @logicalhan 
do we need to react to this or upgrade other prometheus client libraries in concern with this update to 1.0.0?
I count 16 (non-test) locations where we are constructing SummaryOpts without setting Objectives in k/k
Since we own the wrapping layer (i.e. component-base/metrics), we can actually just fallback to the old behavior by defaulting Objectives to whatever DefObjectives was.

lint-dependencies.sh prompts me to upgrade github.com/prometheus/client_golang
```
    pinned:    v0.9.4
    preferred: v1.0.0
    hack/pin-dependency.sh github.com/prometheus/client_golang v1.0.
```

What shall I do?
I have added @logicalhan 's commit for this https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/83987/commits/454a339f3afb9834c52ff5cace40ee6305a75d0c
I changed this part because otherwise it conflict updated prometheous
This will end up being backwards incompatible, since the metrics exposed are actually different.
what's the backwards compatible way to emulate this registration?

Literally copying over the old handler code. I don't think it's worth it though.

While this may break some people's instrumented setups, it breaks a more meta-level of monitoring (scrape frequency and metric endpoint request stuff) and is less critical than control-plane health metrics. 

My preference is to keep @wenjiaswe's changes and have an accompanying release note on the removal of the old prometheus meta-metrics.

> My preference is to keep @wenjiaswe's changes and have an accompanying release note on the removal of the old prometheus meta-metrics.

Ok, I thought you were saying we could not make this change

@logicalhan do you have a suggested release note in mind or could you check what I have below? Not sure how to write release note for breaking changes. Do we include in the PR note or is there a separate place? 

```
Use [promhttp.InstrumentMetricHandler](https://godoc.org/github.com/prometheus/client_golang/prometheus/promhttp#InstrumentMetricHandler) instead of [prometheus.InstrumentHandler](https://godoc.org/github.com/dnesting/client_golang/prometheus#InstrumentHandler) for metrics handler, please refer to the linked doc for the difference.
```

> Ok, I thought you were saying we could not make this change

That is what I was initially thinking, but after looking into the actual metrics this would end up breaking, it seems both low risk/value. 

> do you have a suggested release note in mind

Since we're removing metrics, maybe it would be a good idea to list them? Something like this maybe?
```
Deprecated prometheus request meta-metrics have been removed (http_request_duration_microseconds, http_request_duration_microseconds_sum, http_request_duration_microseconds_count, http_request_size_bytes, http_request_size_bytes_sum, http_request_size_bytes_count, http_requests_total, http_response_size_bytes, http_response_size_bytes_sum, http_response_size_bytes_count) due to removal from the prometheus client library. Prometheus http request meta-metrics are now generated from [promhttp.InstrumentMetricHandler](https://godoc.org/github.com/prometheus/client_golang/prometheus/promhttp#InstrumentMetricHandler) instead.
```
